correctness.rationale: Balanced ternary makes a noncancelling unordered pair of distinct powers (or zero plus a power) unique, with the sole doubled-power carry 2ε3^j=-ε3^j+ε3^(j+1). For D nonzero, the least exponent and residue mod3 reduce all primitive representations by ν3(D), except the three identical-power terms when D=±3^v. After sign normalizing d≡1 mod3, every triple is {1,u,w} with u,w∈{0,±3^j:j>=1} and u+w=d−1≠0, or {-1,-1,w} with w=d+2 in that set. The pair lemma bounds the first family by 2 and second by 1. Equality requires d=1+2ε3^j and d+2 signed 3-power, forcing d=7 or -5 at j=1, plus sign inverses; special D=±3^v has only 2 types. Independent complete finite-depth unordered triple enumerations up to exponent depth 8 give r<=3 with saturation only ±5,±7 times powers of 3. Infinite completeness follows from the residue proof, not finite truncation.
